tool_action.public_message: I can't go below face value for a property that gives you a monopoly. Let's meet in the middle at $225. You get your set, and I get enough cash to stay in the game.
tool_action.private_thought: I need the cash to secure New York Avenue and the Magenta set, but I don't want to sell a set-completer for under face value. Grok has $291, so asking for $225 leaves him with only $66—barely enough to survive a landed rent, and certainly not enough to build on those Reds immediately. It's a safe way to get the liquidity I need.

final_action.public_message: Grok, it looks like your counter-offer got the terms swapped, and $200 is just a bit too low for a property that completes your set. Let's make it easy: $220, which is the exact face value of the property. It gives you the Reds and gives me the liquidity to keep the game moving.
final_action.private_thought: Grok's counter-offer was technically flawed (it suggested I pay him for my own property). I'll correct the terms and meet him halfway. $220 is the face value of Kentucky Avenue. Giving him the Red monopoly is acceptable because he won't have enough cash left to build houses ($71 remaining), while the $220 puts me at $347, ensuring I can secure the final Orange property (New York Avenue) if it becomes available.
